verdict.justification: The visible portions of both workbooks accurately reproduce all nine operators’ Week 1 daily outputs and machine/shift assignments from the reference. Both use appropriate blank-aware formulas, such as “IF(COUNT(E6:I6)=0,"",AVERAGE(E6:I6))”, and leave future daily outputs blank rather than inventing production data. A includes explicit selected-range and YTD helper formulas linked to Dashboard cells, while B presents a simpler data layout and more clearly explains that Average Output means a daily average. Their stated highlighting rules differ—A uses “top 3” and “bottom 3,” whereas B uses “top 2” and “bottom 2”—but either approach meets the requested top/bottom performer emphasis. Both supplied extracts are truncated within the data worksheet, so the actual PivotTables, validation lists, four charts, KPI summary, and full 48-week coverage cannot be compared reliably. On the available evidence, neither has a decisive professional advantage.
